title: [CQ-M04c] Frozen 20-workload baseline execution
definitionOfDone: Exactly 20 outcome records (every frozen workload id, 5 per category, n=1) validate with the CQ-M04 validator; capped/failed runs are present with partial counters, none dropped or silently retried.
The committed report JSON and markdown regenerate byte-identically from the archived records and receipts via `node scripts/analyze-baseline.mjs ... --json` (exit 0).

The report states reproducible inputs (corpus version and per-case digests, Moe commit, per-role model/effort, 60-minute cap) and limitations (n=1, unknown counters, platform coverage); acceptance comes only from held-out assessments, never from Moe task status or token metrics.
Archived records and receipts contain only allowlisted fields (no prompts, tool arguments, secrets or prices), checked by the CQ-M04 validator and the M02 receipt normalizer.
Fresh `node --test scripts/tests/usage-report.test.mjs` exits 0 with output supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: Human-gated operational run: real paid usage and up to ~20 hours wall-clock. Do not start without an explicit human go-ahead recorded on this task.
No reruns beyond n=1; record infrastructure failures, never hide them. Report observed facts only: no savings or significance claims.
No direct .moe edits in the real project; no Git writes outside wrappers; do not enable verified-local or claim isolation.

implementationPlan.description:
Preconditions, environment and batch setup. No paid usage happens in this step.

**1. Gates.** Confirm all of the following.
- CQ-M04b (task-9cfaacf1…), CQ-M04 (task-0ece1a35…) and CQ-M03 (task-cfa74f1b…) are DONE and landed.
- The human go-ahead is on this task: comment-539240c5, relayed by the governor. It says agent-run, in board order, in the background with checkpoints.
- The human configuration is comment-700a6a51 on task-0ece1a35:
  - today's defaults (no settings.models pins; claude seats on claude-opus-5-5, with plan-routing launch hints applying);
  - n=1;
  - a 60-minute cap;
  - capped runs are kept with their partial counters;
  - missing counters stay unknown.
- Read the landed M04b CLI (src/benchmarks/baselineRun.ts and its usage) and the M04 CLI (scripts/analyze-baseline.mjs). Use their landed flags; where they differ from this plan, follow the landed code and say so.

**2. Batch dir.** Create B=/var/tmp/moe-m04c-<YYYYMMDD>. It is durable, outside the repo, and never committed. Keep it until QA approves.

**3. Pinned Moe build.** Archive the commit under test into B/moe:
```
C=$(git -C /mnt/d/projexts/moes rev-parse HEAD)
git -C /mnt/d/projexts/moes archive "$C" packages/moe-daemon packages/moe-proxy docs scripts CLAUDE.md .gitignore package.json | tar -x -C B/moe
```
Then link the Linux node_modules into both packages and build both dists with tsc, exactly as the CQ-M04b gate does. The shared checkout's HEAD moves as peers land, and this archive pins it. Record C.

**4. Preflight.** No real workload is consumed, because every run is n=1.
- `claude --version` works on the Linux-only PATH.
- The machine's Claude accounts are usable. Check this read-only with `node B/moe/packages/moe-daemon/dist/index.js accounts check`, using the same account list this seat uses (its MOE_ACCOUNTS_FILE, else the default).
- The landed M04b focused suite passes in B/moe. It uses the fake CLI with no paid calls, so it is the environment smoke test.
- At least 5 GB is free under /var/tmp.

**5. Manifest.** Generate B/expected.json from the landed M03 corpus via tsx in B/moe: {corpusVersion, workloads: [{id, category, caseDigest: digestWorkload(w)}]} in the corpus order.
- readExpectedManifest must accept it, with 20 ids, 5 per category.
- Write the ids, one per line, to B/ids.txt.

**6. B/batch.sh** (bash; documented later in the archive README; not committed).
- **Single instance and env.**
  - `flock -n` on B/batch.lock, so only one instance runs.
  - Unset every MOE_* variable except MOE_ACCOUNTS_FILE and MOE_SERENA_PATH.
  - Use the Linux-only PATH plus the claude binary's directory.
- **Loop.** For each id in B/ids.txt, in order:
  - If a record for that id already exists anywhere under B/runs, skip it. Records are the source of truth, so a workload is never rerun.
  - If a run root for that id exists WITHOUT a record (a driver crash or reboot), stop the batch with exit 3.
  - Otherwise run the driver from B/moe/packages/moe-daemon: `npx tsx src/benchmarks/baselineRun.ts --workload <id> --cap-minutes 60 --parent B/runs --moe-commit <C>`. Send its output to B/driver-<id>.log, and log UTC start and end plus /proc/loadavg to B/batch.log.
- **Exit codes.**
  - The driver exiting 1 means no run happened: stop with exit 1.
  - A record whose run.status is failed or aborted: log it and stop with exit 2, for triage.
  - A completed or capped record: continue.

**7. Start.** Launch the batch detached with `setsid nohup bash B/batch.sh >> B/batch.log 2>&1 &`. Record its pid and C in the step note.

**Error handling:** any failed precondition stops here, before a single paid run, and is reported with moe.report_blocked naming the failed check.

implementationPlan.description:
Checkpoint 1: wait until the first 5 ids in B/ids.txt have records.

**Waiting**
- Wait in bounded slices. Each check is one Bash call that sleeps at most 9 minutes, then prints only the record count, the batch pid's liveness and the last B/batch.log line. Never dump logs into context.
- About every 3 hours without a checkpoint, post a one-line moe.add_comment progress note, so the governor sees the long-running seat is alive.
- If this session ends, the next session resumes here: the detached batch keeps running and the flock blocks a duplicate.

**Triage when the batch stops before the checkpoint**
- **exit 2** (a failed or aborted record):
  - Read that record's failureReason and the bounded tail of its seat logs.
  - A workload-specific agent failure: leave the record (it is never rerun) and restart the batch.
  - An infrastructure-wide cause (a signed-out account, the daemon cannot start, the disk is full): stop and call moe.report_blocked with the facts, before more paid runs are burned.
- **exit 1** (no run happened): fix the environment cause, note it for the README, and restart the batch. This is not a rerun, because nothing ran.
- **exit 3** (a run root with no record): call moe.report_blocked. The DoD needs 20 records, so a human decides whether that one workload may run once; a silent rerun is forbidden.

**Completion.** Call complete_step with a note listing each of the 5 ids with its run.status and assessment pass/fail/not-run. Report no token or cost conclusions.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
**Chosen: a resumable, single-instance background batch.**
- It runs outside the repo under /var/tmp, against a pinned git-archive build of the commit under test, sequentially in manifest order, with n=1.
- The worker's session waits through four checkpoint steps of 5 records each.
- Step boundaries re-arm MOE_RESUME_MAX_ATTEMPTS, give the account-switch mod a safe point, and leave a visible progress trail. The stale-worker sweep preserves a seat that owns active work.

**Rejected.**
- **Running the driver from the dirty shared checkout.** Its HEAD moves with peers, so the dist would not match the recorded commit.
- **A real-workload smoke run.** It would consume that workload's only run. The fake-CLI M04b suite is the environment smoke test instead.
- **Retrying failed runs.** That is forbidden. Only a run that never started (driver exit 1) may be started again, and the README discloses it.
- **Committing seat logs.** They can hold prompts and tool text.
- **A date-stamped results path.** The task said 'e.g.'; a stable docs/baselines/cq-m04/ path keeps the tests and docs fixed, and the dates go in the README.
- **Heavier routing.** The task is mostly long bounded waiting, so it uses standard/high on Sonnet to keep about 20 hours of polling cheap.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
**The run.**
- The governor relayed the human go-ahead (comment-539240c5): agent-run, in board order, in the background with checkpoints.
- The configuration is comment-700a6a51 on task-0ece1a35.
- The M04b driver (planned) is `npx tsx packages/moe-daemon/src/benchmarks/baselineRun.ts --workload <id> --cap-minutes 60 --parent <dir> --moe-commit <sha>`. It exits 0 once a record is written and 1 when no run happened.
- It writes <runRoot>/records/<id>.json and <runRoot>/usage/<id>/logs/moe-usage.
- analyze-baseline (M04) reads --records, --project (<id>/logs/moe-usage), --expected and --json.

**Receipts.** scripts/usage-receipt.mjs writes rows of exactly:
- version, timestamp and provider;
- the normalizeUsageContext keys (taskId, workerId, role, attemptId, launchId, requestedModel, requestedEffort, launchMode, planRevision, packetId, sourceRetrievalId, plannerInvocationId, runnerId, candidateId, deliveryReceiptId, workKind);
- sessionId, eventId, reportedModels and scope;
- turnIndex (codex only);
- coverage, outcome and usage.

**Long-running seats.**
- The stale-worker sweep keeps a seat that owns active work (state/sweeps.ts), so a long poll is safe.
- moe.heartbeat is wrapper-only, and its sidecar stops after MOE_HEARTBEAT_MAX_DURATION_SEC (2 h). Progress comments are what show the governor the seat is alive.
- MOE_RESUME_MAX_ATTEMPTS is 5, and a completed step re-arms it.

**Machine and test files.**
- Claude accounts here live on the Windows side, under /mnt/c/Users/<user>/.moe/claude-accounts.
- scripts/tests/usage-report.test.mjs is CRLF.
planningNotes.risks:
**Real paid usage of about 20 hours.**
- The account pool is shared with the live fleet. Limit waits count toward the 60-minute cap, so expect some capped runs, and disclose this.
- Contention on the shared WSL machine also affects wall-clock time.

**An infrastructure failure inside a run produces a 'failed' record that cannot be rerun.**
- The batch stops on the first failed or aborted record for triage, and anything infrastructure-wide goes to moe.report_blocked before more runs burn.
- A driver crash with no record (exit 3) needs a human decision, because the DoD requires 20 records.

**Unlanded dependencies.** M04b, M04 and M03 were unlanded at planning time. Use their landed flags and names.
